title: Record the baseline
spec: U02 · read a receipt line by line
intro: Before you optimise anything you need a number to beat. Ask Q9 in naive mode and read the receipt one layer at a time — this is the table every later module has to improve on.
foot: Do it for real: start the bench in replay mode, pin Q9, mode naive · SETUP.md

steps.title: Pin the question
narrative: Q9 is an aggregation question: "Summarize member M-2001's authorization history: how many requests and what were the outcomes?" Answering it correctly requires two specific facts — PA-1001 approved, and PA-1004 in manual review.
It is the question this course returns to most, because aggregation is where naive context assembly looks most defensible: you feel like you need everything. You do not.
steps.youDo: In the Copilot panel, pick Q9 from the standing-questions list and set the mode toggle to naive.

before.title: WHAT A CORRECT ANSWER MUST CONTAIN

cells: the first of M-2001's two requests
the second — an answer that omits it is wrong, however cheap

steps.title: Ask it, and read the bill
narrative: Naive mode does the obvious thing: it puts the whole seeded domain into the prompt and lets the model find the answer. It works. The answer is correct.
Now look at the receipt rather than the answer. 1,700 input tokens, of which 1,612 are retrieved context — the domain dump. The system prompt is 65 tokens and your actual question is 23.
steps.claudeSays: The model reads all 1,612 tokens of retrieved records, finds the two rows about M-2001, and reports them. Every other record was paid for and ignored.

terminal.text: Summarize member M-2001's authorization history: how many requests and what were the outcomes?
assemble(mode=naive) → retrieved: all members, all requests, all criteria

Member M-2001 has 2 authorization requests: PA-1001 APPROVED
(score 100); PA-1004 MANUAL_REVIEW (score 65).

steps.title: Where the money is
narrative: Five layers enter every context window, and on this call one of them is 95% of the bill. That is the whole diagnosis: the retrieved layer is the target, and the other four are rounding errors.
This is why "write a better prompt" is the wrong lever here. Your prompt is 23 tokens. Halving it saves you eleven.

items.label: Retrieved
items.note: 95% of the input — the whole domain, sent to answer one question about one member

steps.title: The number to beat
narrative: Record it. 1,700 input tokens, verified correct, $0.00549. Every strategy in the next twelve modules gets measured against this row, on this question, with the same answer key.

And note the second half of that sentence, because it is the rule the whole course turns on: a strategy that beats 1,700 tokens but drops PA-1004 has not won anything. In U07 you will watch exactly that happen.
steps.youDo: Repeat for all ten standing questions in naive mode and save the table. That is your U02 lab deliverable.
